# Getting an account (your PI must do this) {#sec-account}

::: {.tldr}
You cannot request your own ARCC account. A **PI** (UW faculty or research scientist) must
request it against a specific **project**, in writing. No project means no account — full
stop. Non-UW collaborators get restricted "ARCC-Only" accounts with real limitations. Sort
this out first; it's the #1 thing that blocks new performers for weeks.
:::

## The rule that surprises everyone

On many systems you sign up yourself. **Not here.** ARCC will not create an account without
written confirmation from a Principal Investigator who owns a project. This is deliberate:
accounts are tied to funded projects for accounting and fair-share purposes.

So the actual first step in your ARCC journey is a conversation, not a form:

> "Which project am I being added to, and can the PI email ARCC to add me?"

For ASCEND/ARID performers the project is something like `cowy-firesurro` (the project this
guide was written under). Ask your PI to confirm the exact project name — you will type it
into **every single job** you ever run (@sec-anatomy), so it's worth knowing on day one.

## Who can be a PI

- UW **faculty** (extended-term / tenure-track) or a **Research Scientist**.
- **Not** adjunct, **not** emeritus, **not** a postdoc or student.

If your advisor doesn't qualify, someone who does must sponsor the project. This matters for
a multi-institution engine like ASCEND, where the natural leader of your sub-project might
not be UW faculty.

## UW accounts vs. ARCC-Only accounts

Because ASCEND spans UW, CSU, CU Boulder, Mines, NCAR, and NEON, this distinction will bite
collaborators constantly:

| | Full UW account | ARCC-Only account |
|---|---|---|
| Who | UW-affiliated people | External collaborators without a UW identity |
| HPC (MedicineBow) | ✅ | ✅ |
| GitLab | ✅ | ✅ |
| **Globus data transfer** | ✅ | ❌ **cannot use Globus** |
| Other UW services | ✅ | ❌ |

::: {.callout-warning}
## The collaborator trap
External collaborators on ARCC-Only accounts **cannot use Globus**, which is the
recommended way to move large datasets (@sec-moving-data). They'll need a *guest collection*
set up for them, or a UW person to broker transfers. Plan for this early if your data lives
at CSU or NCAR.
:::

## What you get: the free tier

Each researcher's baseline allocation:

- **100,000 CPU core-hours per year**
- **20,000 GPU-hours per year**

That is a lot for getting started — 100,000 core-hours is roughly one 96-core node running
flat out for six weeks. Investor projects and larger allocations exist beyond this, but you
almost certainly won't hit the free-tier ceiling while you're learning. Core-hours are
counted as (cores × wall-clock hours), which is one more reason not to over-ask for
resources (@sec-resources).

## The practical checklist

1. Confirm with your PI **which project** you're joining and its exact name.
2. Have the **PI email `arcc-help@uwyo.edu`** to request your account on that project.
   (You emailing them yourself won't work — they need the PI's confirmation.)
3. Once ARCC provisions you, you'll get a UW username. **Everything else in this book
   starts from there** — your first login is @sec-first-login.
4. If you're an external collaborator, flag it now and ask how you'll move data, since
   Globus won't be available to you.

No VPN is required to reach ARCC, on campus or off — so once your account exists, you can
log in from anywhere.
